summary: Post-Treaty-of-Waitangi Aotearoa/New Zealand.

name: Polynesian Voyaging & Settlement
summary: A rapid expansion from West to East Polynesia that reached remote islands, including Aotearoa, in the late thirteenth century.

name: Oceanian Prehistory
summary: The Pleistocene settlement of Sahul and the Lapita expansion into the Pacific, gathered here for browsing.

name: Australian Mid-Holocene Intensification
summary: More people, more sites and far more backed artefacts across Australia, tracking the onset of a more variable climate.

name: Bahmani Sultanate
summary: First independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan; the great rival of Vijayanagara.

name: Bengal Sultanate
summary: Independent Muslim sultanate of Bengal; a major trading power in the Indian Ocean.

name: British Raj
summary: Direct British Crown rule of India, 1858–1947.

name: Chalcolithic (South Asia)
summary: The Deccan and central Indian copper-using farming cultures — Kayatha, Ahar-Banas, Malwa and Jorwe — which are not a pre-Bronze stage at all.

name: Chalukyas of Badami
summary: Deccan dynasty that dominated south-central India during the 6th–8th centuries.

name: Western Chalukya Empire
summary: Kalyani-based revival of Chalukya power.

name: Chola Empire
summary: Great Tamil maritime empire; reached Southeast Asia.

name: Deccan Sultanates
summary: Five successor states to the Bahmani Sultanate: Ahmadnagar, Berar, Bidar, Bijapur, Golconda. Together they defeated Vijayanagara at Talikota (1565).

name: Delhi Sultanate
summary: Muslim sultanates ruling northern India from Delhi (1206–1526).

name: Khalji Dynasty
summary: Second Delhi Sultanate dynasty; Turco-Afghan.

name: Lodi Dynasty
summary: Final Delhi Sultanate dynasty; Afghan Pashtuns.

name: Mamluk (Slave) Dynasty
summary: First Delhi Sultanate dynasty; Turkic ex-slave rulers.

name: East India Company Rule
summary: British East India Company ruled increasingly large parts of India from Plassey (1757) to the Government of India Act (1858).

name: Gupta Empire
summary: Classical Indian empire often called the 'Golden Age of India'.

name: Harsha's Empire
summary: Last great pre-Islamic north Indian empire; centered on Kannauj.

name: Hoysala Empire
summary: Karnataka dynasty famed for its ornate temple architecture (Belur, Halebidu).

name: Post-Independence South Asia
summary: Post-1947 independent states of the subcontinent.

name: Prime Ministers of India
summary: Heads of government of the Republic of India from Independence to the present.

name: Leaders of Pakistan
summary: Heads of state and government of Pakistan.

name: Indo-Greek Kingdoms
summary: Greek-speaking kings ruling in Bactria and northwest India after Alexander, issuing bilingual coinage and, in Menander's case, appearing in Buddhist literature as a convert.

name: Indus Valley Civilization
summary: Bronze Age civilization along the Indus and the Ghaggar-Hakra.

name: Kakatiya Dynasty
summary: Telugu dynasty of Warangal; extensive irrigation and temple-building.

name: Mahajanapadas (Second Urbanization)
summary: India's second urbanisation: sixteen or so states across the Ganges plain, some kingdoms and some republics, the setting in which Buddhism and Jainism emerged.

name: Maratha Confederacy
summary: The power that broke Mughal dominance in the Deccan and governed much of the subcontinent through a confederacy of chiefs, until the British defeated it in three wars.

name: Maurya Empire
summary: First empire to unify most of the Indian subcontinent.

name: Mughal Empire
summary: Turco-Mongol Muslim empire that ruled most of South Asia at its peak.

name: Sur Empire (interregnum)
summary: Afghan dynasty that ousted the Mughals for 15 years.

name: Kingdom of Mysore
summary: South Indian kingdom that under Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan resisted British expansion.

name: Pala Empire
summary: Buddhist dynasty of Bengal and Bihar; patronized Nalanda and founded Vikramashila.

name: Pallava Dynasty
summary: South Indian dynasty ruling from Kanchipuram; commissioned the great rock-cut temples at Mahabalipuram.

name: South Asian Prehistory
summary: Early farming, rice cultivation, and pre-urban settlement traditions across South Asia.

name: Rashtrakuta Dynasty
summary: Deccan-based empire that patronized both Hinduism and Jainism; commissioned Kailasa Temple at Ellora.

name: Satavahana Empire
summary: The dominant power of the Deccan between the Maurya and Gupta empires, controlling the trade that carried Roman coinage into central India.

name: Sikh Empire
summary: Ranjit Singh's state in Punjab, which absorbed Kashmir and Peshawar, kept the British at the Sutlej for a generation, and fell within a decade of his death.

name: Southern Neolithic
summary: A separate Neolithic in the South Deccan, built on cattle, native millets and enormous mounds of burnt dung.

name: Vedic Period
summary: The period of the Vedic corpus in northern South Asia, dated from the texts rather than from excavation.

name: The Vedic Corpus
summary: Rigveda, then the other three Vedas, the Brahmanas, and the Upanishads.

name: Aravidu Dynasty
summary: Rump dynasty after the catastrophic defeat at the Battle of Talikota (1565).

name: British Burma
summary: Annexed after the Third Anglo-Burmese War and governed as a province of British India until 1937.

name: Đinh Dynasty
under: Vietnam (dynastic) < Mainland Southeast Asia < Southeast Asia
summary: Declared the state Đại Cồ Việt and an imperial title to match.

name: Dvaravati
summary: Mon Buddhist culture of the Chao Phraya basin, of disputed political unity.

name: Early Lê Dynasty
under: Vietnam (dynastic) < Mainland Southeast Asia < Southeast Asia
summary: Repelled a Song invasion, then gave way to the Lý.

name: French Indochina
summary: The colonial union of Vietnamese, Cambodian and Lao territories.

name: Hồ Dynasty
under: Vietnam (dynastic) < Mainland Southeast Asia < Southeast Asia
summary: Seven years of forced reform; renamed the state Đại Ngu and fell to the Ming.

name: Khmer Empire (Angkor)
summary: Southeast Asia's greatest classical empire. Built Angkor Wat and Angkor Thom.

name: Konbaung Dynasty
summary: The last Burmese dynasty, ended by British annexation after the third of three Anglo-Burmese wars.

name: Lan Xang
summary: Lao kingdom of the middle Mekong, which broke into three rival successor kingdoms.

name: Later Lê Dynasty
under: Vietnam (dynastic) < Mainland Southeast Asia < Southeast Asia
summary: Nominally ruled for three and a half centuries, though for most of them real power lay with the Trịnh and Nguyễn lords.

name: Lý Dynasty
under: Vietnam (dynastic) < Mainland Southeast Asia < Southeast Asia
summary: Two centuries of consolidation; renamed the state Đại Việt in 1054.

name: Mạc Dynasty
under: Vietnam (dynastic) < Mainland Southeast Asia < Southeast Asia
summary: Usurped the throne and held the north, overlapping the Lê rather than succeeding them.

name: Ngô Dynasty
under: Vietnam (dynastic) < Mainland Southeast Asia < Southeast Asia
summary: Founded after Bạch Đằng ended Chinese rule; collapsed into a period of warlords.

name: Nguyễn Dynasty
under: Vietnam (dynastic) < Mainland Southeast Asia < Southeast Asia
summary: The last dynasty; adopted the name Việt Nam, then ruled under French protection from the 1880s.

name: Post-Pagan Burma
summary: Two centuries of competing successor states after Pagan fell, principally Ava in the interior and Hanthawaddy in the delta.

name: Sukhothai Kingdom
summary: Tai kingdom of the upper Chao Phraya, traditionally cast as the first Thai state.

name: Tây Sơn Dynasty
under: Vietnam (dynastic) < Mainland Southeast Asia < Southeast Asia
summary: A rising from the south that swept away the Trịnh, the Nguyễn lords and the Lê, and repelled a Qing invasion.

name: Thonburi Kingdom
summary: Fifteen years under Taksin, between the Burmese sack of Ayutthaya and the founding of the Chakri dynasty.

name: Toungoo Dynasty
summary: Reunified Burma and briefly built the largest empire in mainland Southeast Asia.

name: Trần Dynasty
under: Vietnam (dynastic) < Mainland Southeast Asia < Southeast Asia
summary: Repelled three Mongol invasions.

name: Vietnam (dynastic)
summary: Independent Vietnamese states from the end of Chinese rule to the abdication of the last emperor.

name: Aceh Sultanate
summary: North Sumatran sultanate and a major pepper power, which fought the Dutch for three decades.

name: Bruneian Empire
summary: Bornean sultanate that dominated the northwest coast before contracting under British and Sarawak pressure.

name: Demak Sultanate
summary: The first Islamic state on Java, and the power that finished Majapahit.

name: Republic of Indonesia
summary: Southeast Asian archipelagic republic; world's fourth-most-populous country.

name: Kahuripan
summary: Airlangga's kingdom, divided between his sons at his abdication.

name: Kediri Kingdom
summary: East Javanese kingdom, remembered above all for its literature.

name: Majapahit Empire
summary: Javanese thalassocracy at Southeast Asia's peak of classical influence.

name: Mataram Sultanate
summary: The dominant Javanese state of the 17th century, partitioned under Dutch pressure.

name: Medang Kingdom
summary: The Central Javanese period, which built Borobudur and Prambanan.

name: Singhasari Kingdom
summary: Displaced Kediri and expanded Javanese power outward; ended in the succession crisis that produced Majapahit.

name: Srivijaya
summary: Sumatran maritime empire that dominated the Malacca Strait.

name: Sultanate of Sulu
summary: Sultanate of the Sulu archipelago, which resisted Spanish control for three centuries.

name: Tondo
summary: Polity on Manila Bay, attested from 900 CE by the earliest surviving Philippine document.

name: Southeast Asian Prehistory
summary: The long prehistory of mainland and island Southeast Asia, including cave traditions, metal-age communities, and early human remains.

name: The Austronesian Expansion
summary: From Taiwan to the edge of Remote Oceania: the widest maritime dispersal in prehistory, and one that kept stopping.

name: The Hittites
summary: An Anatolian empire that fought Egypt to a draw at Kadesh and left the oldest surviving international peace treaty.

name: Collapse of the Hittite Empire
summary: The empire dissolves in the first quarter of the 12th century, during a drought that tree rings date to three specific years.

name: Hittite Old Kingdom
summary: Hattusa becomes the capital and Hittite armies reach Babylon.

name: Lydia
summary: A western Anatolian kingdom rich enough on electrum to invent coined money, ending when Cyrus took Sardis.

name: Mitanni
summary: A Hurrian kingdom of northern Syria, rival and then in-law to both Egypt and Hatti, which left the world's oldest horse-training manual.

name: Neo-Hittite States
summary: Luwian- and Aramaic-speaking successor kingdoms that kept Hittite hieroglyphs alive for four centuries after the empire died.

name: Phrygia
summary: An Anatolian kingdom centred on Gordion whose king Midas turns out to be documented in Assyrian records.

name: Urartu
summary: An Iron Age kingdom around Lake Van, Assyria's most persistent northern rival, built on fortresses and irrigation.

name: Dilmun
summary: The Gulf trading power that stood between Mesopotamia and the Indus, and which Mesopotamian literature remembered as a kind of paradise.

name: The Nabataeans
summary: Caravan traders who took the northern end of the incense route, cut Petra out of sandstone, and were annexed by Rome without a fight.

name: Saba
summary: The incense kingdom of the Yemeni highlands, the Sheba of later legend, and the builder of the Marib Dam.

name: Rise of Islam
summary: Muhammad's prophetic career and the birth of Islam.

name: Sea Peoples
summary: A name Egyptian scribes gave to raiders from several origins, tied to the collapse of the Bronze Age eastern Mediterranean.

name: Achaemenid Empire
summary: First Persian empire; largest of its time.

name: Afsharid Dynasty
summary: Nader Shah's conquest state, which outlasted him only in Khorasan.

name: Aq Qoyunlu
summary: Turkoman confederation that displaced the Qara Qoyunlu and was in turn displaced by the Safavids.

name: Buyid Dynasty
under: The Iranian Intermezzo < Iran < West Asia
summary: Shia dynasty from the Caspian highlands that took Baghdad and ruled through the Abbasid caliphs it kept as figureheads.

name: Middle Elamite Period
summary: Elam at its most powerful, building Chogha Zanbil and carrying Babylonian monuments home as loot — including the Code of Hammurabi.

name: Neo-Elamite Period
summary: Elam's last independent centuries, spent largely in coalition against Assyria, and known mostly through Assyrian accounts of defeating it.

name: Old Elamite Period
summary: Elam's first documented dynasties — Awan, Simaški, Sukkalmah — locked in alternating war and marriage with Akkad, Ur and Babylon.

name: The Iranian Intermezzo
summary: Native Iranian dynasties ruling between Arab and Turkic domination.

name: Islamic Republic of Iran
summary: Theocratic state established by Ayatollah Khomeini after the 1979 revolution.

name: Pahlavi Dynasty
summary: Last royal dynasty of Iran; overthrown by the 1979 Islamic Revolution.

name: Parthian (Arsacid) Empire
summary: Iranian empire that ruled Persia and Mesopotamia for four centuries; Rome's chief eastern rival.

name: Qajar Dynasty
summary: The dynasty that lost the Caucasus to Russia, granted the concessions that made Iran a field of Anglo-Russian competition, and was forced into a constitution in 1906.

name: Qara Qoyunlu
summary: Turkoman confederation holding Azerbaijan and western Iran.

name: Safavid Empire
summary: Made Shia Islam the state religion.

name: Saffarid Dynasty
under: The Iranian Intermezzo < Iran < West Asia
summary: Rose from Sistan under a coppersmith turned warlord and briefly threatened Baghdad itself.

name: Sasanian Empire
summary: Last pre-Islamic Persian empire; peer superpower of Rome/Byzantium.

name: Seleucid Empire
summary: Hellenistic successor state to Alexander's eastern conquests; the biggest single Diadochi kingdom.

name: Tahirid Dynasty
under: The Iranian Intermezzo < Iran < West Asia
summary: Governed Khorasan from Nishapur, nominally for the Abbasids and in practice for themselves.

name: Zand Dynasty
summary: Ruled Iran except Khorasan from Shiraz, remembered for an unusually peaceful reign.

name: Akkadian Empire
summary: First empire in world history.

name: Assyrian Empires
summary: Ancient Mesopotamian empires that dominated the Near East in the Iron Age.

name: Middle Assyrian Empire
under: Assyrian Empires < Mesopotamia & Levant < West Asia

name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
under: Assyrian Empires < Mesopotamia & Levant < West Asia
summary: Mass deportations as imperial policy; library of Nineveh.

name: Kingdoms of Israel and Judah
summary: Iron Age Hebrew kingdoms.

name: Kassite Babylon
summary: Four centuries of stable Babylonian rule under a dynasty of foreign origin, during which Babylon became a recognised great power in the diplomacy of the Late Bronze Age.

name: Neo-Babylonian Empire
summary: Chaldean dynasty that overthrew Assyria; Nebuchadnezzar destroyed Jerusalem in 587 BCE.

name: Old Babylonian Empire
summary: Amorite dynasty of Babylon; Hammurabi's law code.

name: Phoenician City-States
summary: Independent Canaanite-speaking city-states on the Levantine coast, never politically unified.

name: Sumerian Early Dynastic
summary: World's first cities: Uruk, Ur, Lagash, Kish.

name: Ur III (Neo-Sumerian)
summary: The last Sumerian-speaking dynasty, which left the earliest surviving law code and an administrative archive of tens of thousands of tablets.

name: West Asian Prehistory
summary: Where farming, villages and monumental building appear first, and hand off to Sumer.

name: Chalcolithic (Southern Levant)
summary: The southern Levantine Copper Age, with copper hoards, ossuary burial and the Ghassulian culture.

name: Chalcolithic (Anatolia)
summary: The Anatolian Copper Age, spanning the long interval between the Neolithic villages and the Early Bronze Age.

name: Epipalaeolithic (Levant)
summary: The long Levantine hunter-gatherer sequence between the Upper Palaeolithic and farming, ending where the Mesolithic begins.

name: Late Chalcolithic (Mesopotamia)
summary: Terminal Ubaid through Late Uruk, the LC1-LC5 sequence that ends with the first cities and the first writing.

name: Uruk Period
under: Late Chalcolithic (Mesopotamia) < West Asian Prehistory < West Asia
summary: The centuries in which southern Mesopotamia produced the first cities, the first bureaucracy, and the first writing.
